paragraphs.text: During Fiscal 2017 and in the context of acquisitions made in Fiscal 2017, we began to implement restructuring activities to streamline our operations (collectively referred to as the Fiscal 2017 Restructuring Plan). The Fiscal 2017 Restructuring Plan charges relate to workforce reductions and facility consolidations. These charges require management to make certain judgments and estimates regarding the amount and timing of restructuring charges or recoveries. Our estimated liability could change subsequent to its recognition, requiring adjustments to the expense and the liability recorded. On a quarterly basis, we conduct an evaluation of the related liabilities and expenses and revise our assumptions and estimates as appropriate.
Since the inception of the plan, $41.9 million has been recorded within "Special charges (recoveries)". We do not expect to incur any further significant charges relating to this plan.

items.question: CJ, KJ, and AJ collect stamps.  CJ has 5 more than twice the number of stamps that KJ has, and KJ has half as many as AJ.  If the three boys have 930 stamps all together, how many stamps does AJ have?

previous_f3_program: collection("three_boys.stamps", "stamp", "three_boys", source("CJ, KJ, and AJ collect stamps"))
member("three_boys.stamps", "cj.stamps", source("CJ, KJ, and AJ collect stamps"))
member("three_boys.stamps", "kj.stamps", source("CJ, KJ, and AJ collect stamps"))
member("three_boys.stamps", "aj.stamps", source("CJ, KJ, and AJ collect stamps"))
offset(at("cj.stamps.count", "current"), scale(at("kj.stamps.count", "current"), 2), 5, "count", source("CJ has 5 more than twice the number of stamps that KJ has"))
fraction_of(at("kj.stamps.count", "current"), at("aj.stamps.count", "current"), 1, 2, source("KJ has half as many as AJ"))
observe(at("three_boys.stamps.count", "current"), 930, "count", source("the three boys have 930 stamps all together"))

sum_relation(at("three_boys.stamps.count", "current"), at("cj.stamps.count", "current"), at("kj.stamps.count", "current"), at("aj.stamps.count", "current"), source("the three boys have 930 stamps all together"))
query("value", at("aj.stamps.count", "current"))

items.question: Magdalena has an apple tree on their farm, producing very few apples each year for a while now. However, this year, the apple tree yield was excellent, and it grew 200 apples. Magdalena picked 1/5 of the fruits on the first day, twice that number on the second day, and 20 more apples than he picked on the first day on the third day. Calculate the total number of apples remaining in the tree.

previous_f3_program: collection("magdalena.apple_tree.apples", "apple", "magdalena.apple_tree", source("it grew 200 apples"))
observe(at("magdalena.apple_tree.apples.count", "initial"), 200, "count", source("it grew 200 apples"))

remove("first_day_pick", "magdalena", at("magdalena.apple_tree.apples.count", "current"), fraction(at("magdalena.apple_tree.apples.count", "initial"), 1, 5), source("Magdalena picked 1/5 of the fruits on the first day"))
remove("second_day_pick", "magdalena", at("magdalena.apple_tree.apples.count", "current"), scale(event_field("first_day_pick", "quantity"), 2), source("twice that number on the second day"))
offset("magdalena.apple_tree.apples.picked.third_day.count", event_field("first_day_pick", "quantity"), 20, "count", source("20 more apples than he picked on the first day on the third day"))

remove("third_day_pick", "magdalena", at("magdalena.apple_tree.apples.count", "current"), "magdalena.apple_tree.apples.picked.third_day.count", source("20 more apples than he picked on the first day on the third day"))
query("remaining_count", "magdalena.apple_tree.apples", "current")
